interaction.prompt: The puck is in the corner and two opponents are getting open near your net. Tap the one your team must cover FIRST — the bigger scoring threat right now.

feedback.right: Yes. That opponent is parked in the slot, right on the doorstep of your goalie. That is the highest-danger ice, so they get covered before the high-slot shooter.
feedback.wrong: The high-slot opponent is a threat, but they are farther out. The opponent on the doorstep is the bigger danger — a pass there is a tap-in. Cover the slot first, then close on the shooter.

tip: When the puck goes to the corner, scan the front of your net first. A player already parked there is a bigger threat than the puck carrier who is stuck in the corner.
why: U11 defenders fixate on the puck and lose track of the slot. This rep trains reading the net-front threat before the pass is made — the whole anticipation skill is seeing where the danger is BEFORE the puck arrives.
